transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-19 15:00 PST / Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Evan Brooks (Redwood AE), Marta Ruiz (Redwood SE), Carlos Menendez (CISO - Sierra), Amrita Patel (Cloud Architect - Sierra), Jared Klein (Security Manager - Sierra), Sofia Ruiz (Compliance Analyst - Sierra), Tom Hargreaves (Procurement - Sierra)
Summary: Walkthrough of Redwood trust center materials, SOC 2/ISO artifacts, RBAC and SSO approach, audit log retention and delivery, and customer-managed KMS options. Goal: determine readiness for pilot and identify evidence needed for Sierra's internal audit.
Topics: SOC 2 Type II availability and scope, ISO 27001 alignment, Trust Center access levels, RBAC/SSO (SAML/OIDC), audit log exports and retention, customer-managed keys (CMEK/HSM), data residency (EU data residency request), dedicated vs hosted deployment tradeoffs.

[00:00] Evan Brooks: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 40 minutes. Quick intros?
[00:12] Carlos Menendez: Carlos, CISO at Sierra. We're doing a compliance gate for an upcoming procurement. Need to validate Redwood's controls mapping to our SOC2 and ISO checklists.
[00:25] Amrita Patel: Amrita, cloud architect, I'll be digging into VPC and KMS details.
[00:33] Marta Ruiz: Hi all, Marta from Redwood, I'll focus on the technical artifacts and integration points.
[00:38] Tom Hargreaves: Tom from procurement, short intro.
[00:42] Evan Brooks: Great. Agenda — we'll show Trust Center, point to SOC 2 artifacts, discuss RBAC/SSO and audit logs, then action items.

[02:05] Marta Ruiz: Opening the Trust Center, note it's read only for external folks, we'll share a redacted SOC2 PDF. The Trust Center has our control mapping spreadsheet. You can see controls grouped by CC and then the corresponding Redwood procedures.
[02:30] Carlos Menendez: Quick question — is the scope full platform or only hosted API? Our procurement prefers SaaS but all data in EU region.
[02:45] Evan Brooks: Good call. For hosted API we support EU region with data residency options; our SOC 2 covers hosted platform operations across primary regions — we'll mark the EU region in the spreadsheet. For private deployments we have additional controls and on-prem packaging.

[04:10] Amrita Patel: For private, do you provide a customer-managed control plane or is it still Redwood managed? We need to know KMS flow specifics.
[04:23] Marta Ruiz: Private can be deployed in VPC with a customer-managed control plane option. For KMS we support both Redwood-managed keys and CMEK via customer KMS (AWS KMS/GCP CMEK). HSM integrations are available for Dedicated with an extra ops agreement.

[05:15] Jared Klein: How are audit logs surfaced? We need immutable logs for at least 7 years and a chain of custody record for certain events.
[05:28] Marta Ruiz: We export control plane and audit logs to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets via secure transfer. Logs include request metadata, model route, token counts, and admin actions. Retention is configurable; default is 90 days but you can set to longer through a retention policy in the Trust Center. For immutable storage we recommend bucket-level object lock + customer-side WORM.

[06:50] Carlos Menendez: Does the exported log include payloads or PII? We need to ensure payloads are redacted unless customer requests otherwise.
[07:04] Evan Brooks: By default payloads are not stored in the control-plane audit logs. We store request metadata; customers can enable optional request/response capture for debugging under an explicit data retention policy — and that would be surfaced in the Trust Center and needs approval.

[08:30] Amrita Patel: On SSO, do you support SAML 2.0 and OIDC? We run Okta and Azure AD.
[08:40] Marta Ruiz: Yes both. We support SAML and OIDC, SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC with role mapping and per-team scopes. There's a nuance: RBAC at the token level can be scoped to routes and models.
[09:04] Carlos Menendez: We have strict separation of duties. Can you show how audit and admin roles are separated?
[09:15] Marta Ruiz: In the console we have built-in roles: Admin, Security Admin, Operator, Read-only. You can create custom roles. Security Admin sees the audit logs and can request exports; Operator can manage workloads but not access billing or Trust Center.

[10:40] Jared Klein: For SOC2 evidence, what's the typical turnaround to provide artifacts like change control logs, patch records?
[10:52] Evan Brooks: For standard requests we provide access to the Trust Center and a redacted evidence bundle — usually 3 business days. For deeper evidence we can coordinate with our compliance team and provide a tailored package.

[12:05] Amrita Patel: Data residency — we need guaranteed EU-at-rest and EU-processing for a subset of customers. How do you guarantee processing locality?
[12:20] Marta Ruiz: Requests are routed to EU-deployed clusters when a workspace is provisioned in EU region. We also support project-level region pinning. For background tasks and tooling that touch metadata we have controls to store those in-region by default for pinned workspaces. We'll surface region routing in the Trust Center.

[13:50] Carlos Menendez: Regarding encryption, is it AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit? Are keys always rotated?
[14:02] Marta Ruiz: Yes AES-256 default at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit. We rotate our service keys per our key rotation policy in the controls doc; for customer-managed keys rotation is customer-controlled, but we support automated key rotation hooks if you want Redwood to trigger a rotation workflow with your KMS.

[15:40] Amrita Patel: Can you show a diagram of the KMS flow for CMEK? We need to map who has access to decrypt live inference requests.
[15:50] Marta Ruiz: (screen shares) The typical flow: customer workspace has CMEK configured -> Redwood runtime requests data key via KMS grants -> ephemeral data key used for disk encryption or envelope encryption for model KV cache. The service does not persist plaintext keys. I'll share the diagram afterwards — note sometimes folks call it the kay-ems flow or kay-v cache in transcripts, we've seen that typo.

[17:05] Tom Hargreaves: If we go hosted, what's the SLA and is it tied to SOC2 coverage? Procurement needs an uptime SLA and credits.
[17:17] Evan Brooks: Hosted API SLA is 99.9% for our paid plans and we offer credits aligned with downtime. Dedicated has a stronger SLA and options for private nodes. SOC2 is about controls and processes not SLA itself but the evidence package will show operational procedures that support uptime.

[18:55] Carlos Menendez: Are you able to do pen tests or share third-party pen test reports? We like to see external test results.
[19:06] Marta Ruiz: We have third-party pen testing annually; we can share the executive summary and remediation plan. Full reports are redacted.

[20:40] Jared Klein: Any vendor lock-in concerns? We're comparing to BigCloudAI and VectraServe — can we export model configs, full logs, and do an orderly offboard?
[20:55] Evan Brooks: Yes, we support full exports of model configs and artifacts; for embeddings we provide export APIs. We also support routing backup to a fallback model — the idea is graceful degradation.

[22:10] Amrita Patel: Network connectivity — do you allow VPC peering or private link?
[22:18] Marta Ruiz: Both. We support AWS PrivateLink, VPC peering, and interconnect options for major clouds. For on-prem we support VPN or direct connect arrangements.

[23:40] Carlos Menendez: A question about logs: are admin actions signed and auditable with user IDs? We need chain of custody for actions like model changes and key rotations.
[23:52] Marta Ruiz: Yes admin actions are recorded with user ID, timestamp, IP, and request ID. For key rotations we record KMS events and link them to the admin action ID.

[25:10] Amrita Patel: For long-term retention (7 years), is Redwood able to retain that or do we need to export to our buckets?
[25:20] Marta Ruiz: We recommend exporting to your S3/GCS with object lock for WORM. Keeping 7 years on Redwood side is possible via extended retention add-on but typically customers keep long-term archives in their own storage.

[26:50] Jared Klein: Compliance mapping — do you provide a control matrix that maps SOC2/ISO controls to Redwood artifacts?
[26:58] Marta Ruiz: Yes the Trust Center contains a controls mapping spreadsheet mapping SOC 2 CCs and ISO 27001 annex controls to Redwood policies and evidence locations.

[28:30] Evan Brooks: Quick roadmap note: for Dedicated we plan to add HSM-as-a-service integrations and extra access logging for 2026-Q1.

[29:12] Carlos Menendez: One more — incident response and notification windows? We need to confirm SLA for incident notification to customers.
[29:23] Marta Ruiz: Incident response follows our IR runbook; for P1 incidents we have 4-hour initial notification, full incident report within 72 hours. We'll include that in the evidence bundle.

[31:05] Amrita Patel: Are there any known gaps for ISO 27001 certification support?
[31:14] Evan Brooks: We are aligned to ISO controls and can provide the mapping; we are not currently ISO-certified for the hosted service in all regions, but we do provide ISO-aligned controls and evidence. We'll surface exact scope in the Trust Center.

[33:00] Carlos Menendez: Okay based on this, next steps for Sierra: need redacted SOC2, KMS diagram, network deep dive, pricing for dedicated pilot, and our questionnaire.

[34:10] Evan Brooks: Recap: we'll share documents, Marta will do the KMS doc, we'll schedule a 60-minute on-prem/dedicated feasibility call with Amrita and infra. Customer to return questionnaire and evidence list.

[35:00] Sofia Ruiz: Quick note — we require proof of point-in-time backups for model artifacts. Is that supported?
[35:12] Marta Ruiz: Yes backups are kept and snapshot metadata is retained; we'll provide the snapshot retention policy details in the evidence bundle.

[36:20] Tom Hargreaves: From procurement side we'll need the standard terms and a data processing addendum (DPA).
[36:30] Evan Brooks: We'll include the DPA and sample MSA; legal will reach out if modifications are needed.

[38:05] Carlos Menendez: Any blockers today? Not yet — we need to see the artifacts and the KMS flow.

[38:20] Evan Brooks: Sounds good. I'll send the SOC2 and Trust Center link after the call, and Marta will drop the KMS diagram. Scheduling invite for the deep dive will go out today.

[40:00] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: some words auto-transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "kayv cache" for KV cache, "Redwood dedicate" for Redwood Dedicated), names occasionally misattributed.
